title: SDK Integration Greensheet — playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, pragmatic playbook for running a 60–90 minute integration lab for new SDK adopters (internal or customer-facing). Target outcome: developer has a working sample app, telemetry flowing to Redwood Console, and a short list of easy next steps. This is intentionally a lightweight, reproducible script (greensheet) — easy to run and easy to copy into customer playbooks.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: engineers pairing with a developer-advocate or solutions engineer; also usable as a 1:many workshop script.
- Scope: onboarding to Redwood SDKs (polyglot), first integration, and essential observability/telemetry checks. Not a replacement for full SDK docs.

High-level flow (60 minutes recommended):
1) 0–5m: quick intro + goals + account/keys sanity check
2) 5–15m: project skeleton and dependency install (Node + Python variants)
3) 15–30m: make first API request (text generation) & handle streaming response
4) 30–45m: add retries, basic error handling, and local fallback (stub)
5) 45–60m: wire telemetry events and verify in Redwood Console; review performance signals
6) 60–75m: optional: embedding example + simple reranking flow, cleanup + next steps

Pre-work checklist (what facilitator asks dev to do ahead):
- Sign up for Redwood account and create an API key (or bring customer key).
- Install Node 18+ and Python 3.10+ locally.
- Git clone repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-sample-starters (branch: lab-stable).
- Have terminal and editor open.

Quickstart commands (copy-paste friendly):
- git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-sample-starters && cd sdk-sample-starters/quick-chat
- npm install (or pnpm i)
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-test-XXXX  # mac/linux (Windows: setx)
- node run-first-call.mjs

First-call expectations (what they should see):
- Successful 200 response with 'choices' or streaming tokens visible
- Console log: request_id: <uuid> and latency_ms ~ 50–800ms depending on model/region
- Redwood Console: new telemetry event within 30–90s visible under dev workspace

Minimal code snippet (copyable) - Node (pseudo):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const r = await client.text.generate({ model: 'redwood-mini-1', prompt: 'Write a haiku about coffee' });
console.log(r.choices[0].text);

Safety + failure handling (simple patterns to teach):
- Detect 429 -> exponential backoff (initial 100ms) + jitter; give user-friendly message
- Detect 5xx -> retry x2 then fallback to cached/ stubbed reply
- Streaming aborted by client -> increment telemetry fallback_count and log trace id

Telemetry checklist (what we wire during the lab):
- Instrument event: sdk.request.start (tags: model, region, route)
- Instrument event: sdk.request.end (tags: lat_ms, status_code, token_count)
- Instrument event: sdk.fallback.used (tags: reason)
- Log helpful metadata: request_id, route, model_variant, commit_sha (from sample app repo)
- Verify events appear in Console: filter by request_id from logs printed locally

Acceptance criteria for the lab (how facilitator passes/fails):
- Developer runs first call and sees generated tokens (manual pass)
- At least one telemetry start/end event surfaces in Console within 2 minutes
- App recovers from an induced 5xx when instructor triggers the failure (show fallback path)

Safety nets & fast recovery (notes-to-self):
- If participant's key is rate-limited, switch to local stub runner: node stub-server.mjs then set REDWOOD_API_URL=http://localhost:8080
- If streaming hangs: ctrl-c, rerun with --no-stream flag to get whole response sync
- Keep a backup key (dev-infra temporary) for facilitators to share in emergencies

Mini-lab variants (15m each):
- Embeddings quick add: compute vectors for 3 sample docs, store in in-memory array, run cosine search and show results
- Rerank demo: call text.generate for short descriptors + embed + simple dot-product rerank for top-3
- Low-bandwidth demo: show batch inference (2–4 queries) to demonstrate throughput improvements

Facilitator script (prompts & callouts):
- "If you get an auth error, first check REDWOOD_API_KEY env var; paste show me the output of echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY (or set)."
- "We expect Console telemetry to lag by up to 90s; don’t panic if it doesn’t appear instantly."
- "When we induce a 500, we’re testing your retry/backoff policy — this is intentional."

Open questions and follow-ups (to track in ENG-redirect board):
- Should we publish a one-click cloud-runner for the lab (gist + ephemeral token)?
- Can we add a quick health-check endpoint sample that pings Redwood Console SLOs?
- Draft a condensed one-pager for sales to run a 20-minute try-it session (ask GTM team).

Measurable success metrics (post-lab):
- % of participants with first-call success within 10m > 85%
- Telemetry events per lab >= 2 (avg)
- Follow-up adoption: number of repos that open PRs to add SDK after lab within 14 days

Rollout timeline (next two sprints):
- Sprint A (2 weeks): finalize scripts, add embeddings variant, produce 1-page cheat sheet
- Sprint B (2 weeks): record a 12-minute walkthrough video, create 1-click cloud runner prototype

Files in sample repo to point at during lab:
- /quick-chat/run-first-call.mjs (first-call example)
- /quick-chat/stub-server.mjs (local stub runner)
- /quick-chat/telemetry-checklist.md (console verification steps)

Owner & escalation:
- Primary owner: Asha Patel (eng-developer-experience)
- Backup: Diego Morales (solutions-eng)
- Escalation to infra: Marcus Green (eng-infra)

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Keep the sample prompts short (<= 30 tokens) to reduce token costs during public workshops
- Keep default model conservative for cost (redwood-mini-1) but call out upgrade path to large models in appendix
- Consider a "no-internet" variant for on-site workshops using the stub runner + canned responses

Revision history:
- 2025-03-10: initial draft (Asha)
- 2025-03-12: added telemetry checklist + sample commands (Diego)
- 2025-03-18: polished facilitator script and acceptance criteria (Rina)

Appendix (helpful links & snippets):
- GitHub starter repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-sample-starters/tree/lab-stable
- Telemetry dashboard template (Console): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/template/sdk-lab-quick
- Minimal Node example (full file): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-sample-starters/quick-chat/run-first-call.mjs

-- end greensheet --

(Informal: this is intentionally minimal — treat as a copyable script for SRE, SEs, advocates. Save a copy and adapt to the customer environment. TODO: convert into short slides for 30m workshop.)
